clue.text: Flag obtained from Jack, Oliver, and another guy

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
a familiar short form of the name Oliver
Roger is another man's name

explanation.surface: A flag handed over by three men, Jack, Oliver and a third chap.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and 'and' make it read as a list of people; each name is shrunk or kept to build the flag's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the skull-and-crossbones banner flown by pirate ships.

clue.text: Frenchman's trousers?

parts.note: Jean is a common French man's name
the possessive ending supplies the final letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether some trousers belong to a man from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as JEAN'S, the Frenchman's possession; the question mark flags the pun on the denim garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeans are denim trousers, so the plural noun matches the garment.

clue.text: Left a runner holding queen's office equipment

indicators.note: something holding another thing has it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written
a sprinter is a fast runner
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A departing athlete carrying away some of the queen's office kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed, but it is the direction abbreviation; the 's after queen is just a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer is a common machine found in offices for producing documents.

clue.text: Pine cut short for a period of time

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, so the end is dropped

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A pine tree felled early in its life, a span of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' suggests the tree, but it is the verb meaning to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a twelve-month span, a standard unit measuring elapsed time.

clue.text: Fancy a tenor badly

indicators.note: done badly suggests the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who has a crush on a singer, despite how poorly he sings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning to be attracted to; it is the adjective meaning elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is what fancy describes as an adjective.

clue.text: Mythical city found in field or a dockland

indicators.note: something found in these words sits inside them, running across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run from the end of field through to the start of dockland

explanation.surface: A legendary city turns up in a meadow or a dockside area.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary South American city of gold sought by conquistadors.

clue.text: Region containing Peru has Inca material all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so the letters are in disorder

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A part of the world including Peru is strewn with Inca artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is one of the countries of Latin America, the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking south of the Americas.

clue.text: Publication to acquire something attractive?

parts.note: short for magazine
to net is to gain or obtain

explanation.surface: A magazine's aim of getting hold of an appealing feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading of attractive: a magnet physically attracts metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet draws iron towards it, so it is literally a thing that attracts.

clue.text: Don't drink at basin for a change

indicators.note: making a change means the order of the letters is altered

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A warning not to drink from a washbasin, just this once.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, especially from alcohol, matching the command not to drink.

clue.text: A bit of whisky, say, before a play

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, whisky being an example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wee whisky ahead of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'A' belongs to the measure of whisky; only the second 'a' joins the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play performed on stage, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Hurting Greek god's back

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A Greek deity complaining that his back aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' seems to be the god's body part; it signals the reversal, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means painful or aching, the adjectival sense of hurting.

clue.text: Leo possibly stirred tsar's gin

indicators.note: something stirred is mixed up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man named Leo mixing the Russian emperor's gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo looks like a man's name, perhaps a Russian, but it is the zodiac lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Queen, perhaps, at home with a large Catholic leader

parts.note: a queen is an example of a playing card
someone at home is in
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A monarch staying home with a senior figure of the Roman church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' points to royalty, but here it is a court card.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is a senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church, ranking just below the Pope.

clue.text: Tiara moved around lobbies

indicators.note: things moved around end up in a new order

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A jewelled headpiece carried from one entrance hall to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobbies' could be a verb about campaigning; here it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria is the plural of atrium, a central hall or entrance court of a building.

clue.text: Surprise attack in the morning north of outback

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, marks morning times
the Australian outback is also called the bush

explanation.surface: An ambush launched at dawn somewhere above the Australian interior.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'north of' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is an attack sprung unexpectedly from a concealed position.

clue.text: Silly to accept ultimately poor sketch

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: daft means silly

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the final letter of poor

explanation.surface: Someone foolish enough to approve a sketch that ends up bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a rough preliminary version or outline, much like a sketch.

clue.text: Beautiful perfume reduced by one hundred

indicators.note: something reduced is made shorter, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a scent is a perfume
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A lovely fragrance diluted a hundredfold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced by one hundred' reads as a single instruction; actually 'reduced' trims the perfume and 'by' places it next to one and hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic describes views or landscapes that are picturesque, i.e. beautiful to look at.

clue.text: Saint who's after some eggs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the founder of Western monasticism
second meaning: the name that follows eggs in a brunch dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Who's after some eggs' sounds like someone hungry; it means the word that comes after 'eggs' in the dish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: St Benedict founded the Benedictine order, and eggs Benedict is poached eggs with hollandaise on a muffin.

clue.text: Rule announced for horse riding gear

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: to reign is to rule as a monarch

explanation.surface: A regulation declared about the kit used when riding horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is the strap a rider uses to steer a horse, part of its tack.

clue.text: Dane confused about king not wearing anything

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another
confused means muddled, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: a person from Denmark, used as letters to rearrange
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A puzzled Dane wondering why the king has no clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the emperor's new clothes, apt for a Danish tale by Hans Christian Andersen.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means unclothed, the state of having nothing on at all.

clue.text: Skewer bananas upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry turning something upside down reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: bananas and bats both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Spearing bananas while holding them the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit but is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab is to pierce with a pointed object, as a skewer does.

clue.text: Rents dilapidated part of ship

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Tears in a rundown section of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear section of a boat or vessel.

clue.text: Quibble with returning metal tool

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: tin is a metallic element
a pick is a digging tool

explanation.surface: An argument over a metal tool that keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, i.e. to quibble.

clue.text: American predator beginning to disturb pirate

parts.note: the black bear is a North American carnivore

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so just that one is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of disturb

explanation.surface: A wild American hunter starts to bother a buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackbeard was the nickname of Edward Teach, a notorious 18th-century pirate.
